_readme: Edit this file to publish progress. Redeploy and the page updates. Nothing else needs touching. Newest entry goes FIRST in the entries array.

status.note: One drink, end to end. Liquid shader and pour transfer working; sealer and scoring next.

entries.title: The liquid reads correctly when you tilt it
entries.body:
The clip-plane approach is holding up. The surface stays flat in world space no matter how the cup rotates, which was the whole reason not to just scale a mesh on Y.

Wobble is driven from the cup's velocity and angular velocity, damped in C# and fed to the shader as two sine offsets. It settles in about a second, which feels right — any faster and it reads as stiff, any slower and it looks like syrup.

Band count is capped at four. Tried six and the drink became unreadable at arm's length, which is exactly the failure the design doc predicted.
bullets: Clip plane holds flat through full cup rotation
Four visible bands maximum, merging logic handles the rest

entries.title: Pour transfer works across the whole chain
entries.body:
IContainer is now implemented by cups, shakers, pitchers and the floor drain. You can brew into a pitcher, chill it, then pour that pitcher into a cup, and the ingredient identity, temperature and batch freshness survive the entire chain.

Spills work by exception rather than by special case: if the downward spherecast hits anything that is not an IContainer, it is a spill. That one decision removed a lot of code I thought I would have to write.
bullets: Flow rate curves by tilt angle
Temperature averages by volume on merge
Spill detection falls out of the same cast

entries.title: Foundation done — and the scorer has tests before it has a station
entries.body:
Assembly definitions are in from day one. Boba.Simulation has zero Unity scene dependencies, which means the quality scorer, freshness curves and economy all run as plain C# under the test framework without entering play mode.

Wrote the scorer first, tested it against fabricated drinks, and only then started building anything that could physically make one. Recommend this order to anyone doing a crafting sim.
bullets: Nine asmdefs, Simulation isolated from UnityEngine
Quality scorer covered by edit-mode tests
